name: Task/part-time job: deposit, fake earnings, blocked withdrawal, more payment
description: An easy-income or task-completion lure leads to a deposit or commission, displays fake earnings, then blocks the withdrawal unless a further fee, tax or top-up is paid. The discriminating step is the blocked withdrawal tied to a further-payment demand — not the job framing.

source_references.document_ref: CybercrimeInformation-135 (original PDF unavailable) — rebound to official replacement pair

manual_retrieval.locator: PIB_MHA_Task_Based_Part_Time_Job_Fraud_2023.pdf p.1 (commission -> more investment -> frozen deposit); I4C_Fake_CAPTCHA_Filling_Jobs_2025.pdf p.1 (denied withdrawal -> further payment)
manual_retrieval.notes: Original SRC-015 PDF still unavailable — NOT resurrected. Two official issuing-body documents together substantiate the full chain; each individually is PARTIAL_OF_COMPOSITE, so claim_match records the pair, not an over-claimed FULL.

explanation.plain: A task or part-time job asked you to deposit money to earn more, then blocked your withdrawal until you pay a fee or tax. That is the trap: the 'earnings' are fake and every payment is lost. A real job never asks you to pay to get paid.
explanation.technical: Task/earning lure + a deposit/fee + a blocked-withdrawal-with-further-payment pretext, spanning pretext, payment and pressure classes. Substantiated by the PIB-2023 + I4C-2025 official replacement pair.
verification_steps: Stop paying immediately — a blocked withdrawal that needs another payment is the scam confirming itself.
Report to the 1930 cybercrime helpline; do not send the 'release fee'.
explanation.why_confidence_limited: Held at APPROVED, not PUBLISHED: the full deposit -> fake-earnings -> blocked-withdrawal chain usually spans several messages, so TrustLens can only partially observe it from a single submission (implementability PARTIAL). Evidence itself is SUPPORTED via the official replacement pair.
